reason: §453 quotes Lully's Codicillus verbatim: 'as Jesus Christ... took on human nature for the deliverance and redemption of mankind... so likewise in our art that which has been wrongfully defiled... is absolved by its opposite.' The alchemist's own comparison of the opus with Christ's redemptive work; direction, attribution, and jung-quotes-source are correct.

§456 gives the Zosimos passage verbatim: 'Jesus Christ made himself one with Adam and bore him up to that place where the Men of Light dwelt before.' Direction (Christ acting on Adam) and attribution to Zosimos are correct; jung-quotes-source fits Jung's literal translation.

§505 quotes the anonymous Liber de arte chymica verbatim: 'it is not without good reason that Mercurius is made equal [non immerito... aequiparatur] to the most glorious and worshipful Virgin Mary.' Subject/object direction matches the aequiparatio as stated; jung-quotes-source correct.

§508 quotes the pseudo-Valentinus 'Allegoria sanctissimae trinitatis': Christ 'died of his own free will, and rose again... So, too, is the gold... it dies and rises again, glorious and redeemed.' The ellipses are faithful; the alchemist's gold-Christ direction is preserved and jung-quotes-source with Basilius Valentinus attribution is correct.

§509 quotes the Wasserstein der Weysen verbatim: 'the terrestrial Philosophical Stone is a veritable Harmonia, Contrafactur, and Prototype of the true spiritual and heavenly Stone Jesu Christ.' The text itself runs terrestrial stone -> prototype of Christ, so the direction is exactly as the source asserts; jung-quotes-source correct.

§512 ends the Orthelius quotation with 'to produce a quintessence whose action may be compared with that of Christ upon mankind' verbatim. Direction (quintessence compared with Christ) and jung-quotes-source attribution to Orthelius are correct.

§512 (Orthelius): 'They say this spirit proceeded from thence... became corporeal, and is the chief constituent of the Saviour [salvatoris] or Philosophical Stone.' The ellipsis is faithful and the direction (spiritus mundi as constituent of the lapis) matches; the doctrine sits inside Orthelius's exposition, so jung-quotes-source/Orthelius is the right attribution.

§474 states verbatim: 'The filius philosophorum is here identified with the "bridegroom" who, as we know, is interpreted as Christ,' within a passage Jung explicitly frames as listing lapis-Christ parallels in Aurora consurgens. jung-reports-parallel with Aurora attribution is correct.

§483, discussing Melchior's hymn to Mary, says verbatim: 'In any case the Virgin is identified with the arcanum of the art.' Subject, direction, source (Melchior Cibinensis), and jung-reports-parallel are all correct.

§465, on the Aurora consurgens author ('evidently a cleric'), states verbatim: 'Alchemy is for him absolutely identical with the Sapientia Dei.' Jung reporting the author's equation; jung-reports-parallel with 'author of Aurora consurgens' is correct.

§476 states verbatim that 'Christ is identified with the homo philosophicus,' and Jung says this connection runs 'through the quotation in Senior,' so the Senior attribution is right; jung-reports-parallel fits.

§453 states verbatim: 'In the writings of the somewhat later Jakob Böhme... the stone has already become a metaphor for Christ.' Jung reporting the stone->Christ metaphor in Boehme's writings; direction and jung-reports-parallel are correct.

§489 states verbatim that Melchior 'felt the alchemical process to be the equivalent of the transubstantiation in the Mass.' The 'felt-as-equivalent-of' relation preserves Jung's careful wording (Melchior placed the transmutation near the Credo, not in place of the Consecration); jung-reports-parallel correct.

§453: 'when we come to the original basic ideas of alchemy we find elements that derive from pagan, and more particularly from Gnostic, sources' — Jung's own thesis, stated in his voice; jung-asserts and direction correct.

§461 states verbatim, in Jung's own voice, that 'the lapis-Christ parallel of the scholastic alchemists had a pagan Gnostic precursor and was by no means a mere speculation of the Middle Ages.' jung-asserts correct.

§462: 'The oldest source to treat specifically of the stone's connection with Christ would appear to be... Pretiosa margarita novella, written by Petrus Bonus of Ferrara.' 'Gives-earliest-treatment-of' preserves 'treat specifically' and so does not collide with §453's Lully as oldest testimony; medium confidence appropriately reflects Jung's hedge ('would appear'). jung-asserts correct.

§459 is Jung's own commentary: 'Prometheus and Epimetheus represent the inner and outer man, like Christ and Adam' — mapping Christ to the inner man and Adam to the outer. Direction and jung-asserts correct.

§476, in Jung's commentary voice: the homo philosophicus 'is also the everlasting inner man, identical or at least connected with the Anthropos.' The hedged relation label mirrors Jung's own hedge; jung-asserts correct.

§497: the Malachi passage 'helped to put the early worship of Christ as Helios or Sol on a rational basis — a tendency that St. Augustine still had to combat.' Jung asserts this historical worship as fact; direction and jung-asserts correct.

§511, Jung's own conclusion: alchemy's ultimate aim 'was trying to produce a corpus subtile, a transfigured and resurrected body.' The paragraph's term is corpus subtile, but Jung's gloss ('transfigured and resurrected body'; cf. glorificatum §462, homo glorificatus §508) is precisely the glorified-body concept the corpus-glorificationis node denotes; jung-asserts correct.
